# EU countries and the euro
Bulgaria joined the European Union on 1 January 2007 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.

Croatia joined the European Union in 2013 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2023.

Hungary joined the European Union in 2004 and is currently preparing to adopt the euro.

Lithuania joined the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2015.

Malta joined the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2008.

Romania joined the European Union on 1 January 2007 and has committed to adopt the euro once it fulfils the necessary conditions.

Slovakia joined the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2009.

# History of the euro
## Recession era
### Lithuania
On 23 July 2014 [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania) became the last [Baltic state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_state) to gain permission to join the euro, which was adopted on 1 January 2015.

### Croatia
[Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia) adopted the euro on 1 January 2023, making it the 20th member state of the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone).

Croatia completed its plans to adopt the Euro Currency as soon as possible after the [1 July 2013 EU accession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_enlargement_of_the_European_Union).

### Bulgaria
[Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria) adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, making it the 21st member state of the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone).
